record.paper_title: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models
record.original_question: For super-linear preferential attachment trees with fitness, determine the correct normalization of the empirical degree distribution and identify its scaling limit.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7 What is the correct scaling of the empirical degree distribution, and what is its scaling limit?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a sequence of random trees $(T_n)_{n\geq 1}$ grown by the following super-linear preferential attachment with fitness rule. Fix a weight function $w:\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\to (0,\infty)$ that is super-linear in the sense that $\sum_{k\geq 0} 1/w(k) < \infty$, and a probability distribution $\mu$ on $(0,\infty)$ (the fitness distribution). Start with $T_1$ a single root vertex assigned an independent fitness drawn from $\mu$. Given $T_n$, the tree $T_{n+1}$ is obtained by attaching a new vertex (whose fitness is drawn independently from $\mu$) to an existing vertex $v\in T_n$ with probability proportional to $f_v \, w(\deg_{T_n}(v))$, where $f_v$ is the fitness of $v$ and $\deg_{T_n}(v)$ its degree in $T_n$.

For each $n$ and $k\geq 0$ let
$$N_k(n) \;=\; \#\{v\in T_n : \deg_{T_n}(v)=k\}$$
denote the empirical degree count, and consider the empirical degree distribution $(N_k(n)/n)_{k\geq 0}$.

Find a deterministic normalization $a_n(k)$ (possibly depending on $k$ as well as $n$) such that, as $n\to\infty$, the rescaled empirical degree counts $N_k(n)/a_n(k)$ converge to a non-degenerate limit, and identify this scaling limit explicitly as a stochastic process or random measure in $k$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in a survey of open problems in stochastic reinforcement models. Searches reveal related work on fitness/aging in (sub- or asymptotically linear) preferential attachment trees and on explosiveness of super-linear branching processes, but no result identifying the correct normalization and scaling limit of the empirical degree distribution in the super-linear-with-fitness regime. No resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: The Dynamics of Power laws: Fitness and Aging in Preferential Attachment Trees
status_evidence.snippet: Power-law degree distributions in preferential attachment trees with asymptotically linear weights, fitness, and aging; super-linear weights imply explosiveness.
status_evidence.claim: Related results treat asymptotically linear weights with fitness; super-linear case is qualitatively different and not covered.

status_evidence.title: Connectivity Transitions in Networks with Super-Linear Preferential Attachment
status_evidence.snippet: Studies condensation/persistent hub phenomena under super-linear preferential attachment.
status_evidence.claim: Super-linear preferential attachment is known to produce condensation, but empirical degree distribution scaling limits with fitness are not characterized.
